text:
IncidentBot: Pager alert: dedicated-pool 'calderahealth-prod' high GPU utilization -> 95% across pool, queueing increasing. P50 latency 120ms, P99 1.8s. Paging on-call (severity: SEV2).
Raj (on-call): I'm on it. Pulling pool metrics + queue. @Leo can you confirm autoscale/burst config for that pool?
Leo (infra): Affirm. Pool is set with burst disabled by default for enterprise tenants. Current config: min=4, max=12, reserved=6. Autoscaler at 100% utilization threshold. Seeing sustained 96% for ~6m.
Emily (SRE): Copy. Any customer-facing errors? Nina, can CalderaHealth confirm if they're seeing errors or degraded throughput on their side?
Nina - CalderaHealth: We're seeing requests queueing and timeouts ~3-5% of requests. UI reports slow completions. Impacting nightly ingestion jobs. We're pausing non-critical batches now.
Raj (on-call): Ok customer impact confirmed. I'm going to evaluate quick mitigations: 1) enable emergency burst to add 2 GPUs temporarily; 2) evict low-priority tenants from that rack; 3) fallback routes -> model variant with lower memory. Thoughts?
Marta (eng): Enabling emergency burst is fastest. Evictions require coord with scheduler and will risk churn. If we burst + enable prefix KV caching, we should regain headroom.
Leo (infra): To enable burst I need approval from on-call lead or incident commander. Burst will allocate from spare capacity pool — can last up to 30m auto-shrink. Risk: could push other soft-tenant workloads to queued state for a bit.
Raj (on-call): I approve emergency burst for 30m. Prioritize keeping Caldera's SLA. @Victor please prep the burst: `poolctl burst --pool calderahealth-prod --add 2 --duration 30m`.
Victor (ops): Running command now. Output:
```
> poolctl burst --pool calderahealth-prod --add 2 --duration 30m
Applying burst: +2 GPUs -> new max=14
Allocating nodes: node-gpu-187, node-gpu-192
Burst applied at 1767772348
```
IncidentBot: Burst applied by Victor at 1767772348. Autoscaler state: suspended for pool. Notifying other tenants of potential transient pressure.
Marta (eng): Also enabling prefix KV caching for Caldera's common prompts to reduce token work. Pushing small config change to runtime: `cache.prefix.enable=true` for that route.
Raj (on-call): Patch applied? What's the effect on latency/queueing?
Leo (infra): After burst and cache toggle: queue length dropped 70%, P50 40ms, P99 350ms. Still watching for any retention of load after 10m. CPU on nodes OK, memory stable.
Nina - CalderaHealth: Confirmed improvements — timeouts dropped to ~0.2%, ingestion resumed. Thank you — will monitor.
Raj (on-call): Good. Next steps: 1) keep burst for full 30m window, 2) engage capacity planning for customer's growing footprint (recommend reserved + higher reserved cap), 3) follow-up postmortem if recurring. @Marta please start a ticket for model caching audit.
Marta (eng): Created ticket CM-4821 "CalderaHealth runtime caching audit" and assigned to runtime team. ETA initial findings 48h.
Leo (infra): I'll schedule a capacity review with sales/CS to discuss dedicated sizing vs. burst reliance. Suggest reserved=8 and max=16 for this profile.
Raj (on-call): Handoff: I'm signing out in 15m. @Emily you'll be taking over monitoring and will coordinate with CS for customer comms. Key things to watch: queue length, P99, and burst expiry at 1767774148.
Emily (SRE): Ack. I'll watch and set autoscribe alerts at P99>800ms. Preparing a short customer message for CS: "We've applied a temporary capacity increase and caching optimization — service should be stable; we're investigating long-term sizing." Will loop in Nina as we finalize.
Nina - CalderaHealth: Appreciate the quick response. We'll await the sizing proposal. Please keep us posted before burst expiration.
Raj (on-call): Note for post-incident: check why autoscaler didn't trigger earlier — logs show sustained spike but scaler threshold may have been pinned. Adding investigation to playbook.
Victor (ops): Burst expiration reminder set for 1767774148. I will auto-shrink then unless we extend.
IncidentBot: SEV2 -> status: mitigated. Time to mitigate: 4m from page to burst application. Tickets: CM-4821. Incident commander: Raj. On-call handoff at 1767772680.
Emily (SRE): Taking over now. Logging final snapshot and will update CS channel with blurb. Closing incident thread after follow-up actions scheduled. :white_check_mark:
